practices_report.description: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior.
Test cases should not depend on other tests or on execution order.

practices_report.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_report.description: Test cases must check both normal and edge case scenarios.
Tests should validate inputs at minimum, maximum, and just outside boundaries.
Tests should be self-contained and reusable; extract repeated setup into helpers.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep test cases small and focused; avoid unnecessary complexity.
Assertions should be comprehensive and verify all relevant properties of the result.
Avoid @Ignore or commented-out tests; keep test code active and runnable.
Each test should be linked to a requirement via annotations or Javadoc.

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Performance and security must be tested separately from functional tests.
Test names should describe the scenario and the expected outcome.

practices_report.description: Generated test code should be minimal and focused; avoid verbose auto-generated tests.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_report.description: Prioritize test cases and use TDD/BDD patterns; include Given-When-Then structure where appropriate.

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_report.description: Tests should focus on public APIs and avoid testing implementation details.
Use specific assertions with descriptive messages rather than generic ones.
Comments should explain 'why' not 'what' and should be minimal and useful.
Avoid randomness, current time dependencies, and external non-mocked systems.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_report.description: Tests must not modify shared state and should clean up resources after execution.
